objective: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.
objectiveFingerprint: become campaign card day eligible emi history no plan purchases

questions.text: When you say you want more EMI-eligible purchases to convert, do you mean the most number of transactions converted, or the most value/revenue shifted onto EMI (even if that means fewer but larger conversions)?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If it's count of conversions, the campaign targets the broadest eligible base and optimises for easy, frequent conversions — smaller ticket sizes, simpler nudges.
contingency.ifB: If it's value/revenue, the campaign should weight toward higher-ticket eligible transactions and customers likely to carry larger balances, even though there are fewer of them.
contingency.ifUnknown: Assume count of conversions is the primary read, since that is the more common operational target, but flag that value is not being optimised.

questions.text: Have you noticed any pattern in who already converts an eligible purchase to EMI versus who doesn't — for example anything about the type of purchase, the customer, or when it happens?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If you've seen a pattern, I use it to decide who the campaign should prioritise and what the message should address.
contingency.ifB: If you haven't tracked it or don't know, I treat this as unknown and design the first run to also test a couple of plausible splits rather than assume one.
contingency.ifUnknown: If you genuinely don't know, I'll propose testing two or three plausible customer splits in this first run so we learn rather than guess.

questions.text: What's stopping the rest of the eligible purchases from converting, in your view — do customers not notice the option, think it costs too much, find it a hassle to set up, or something else?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: If it's awareness, the campaign leads with simple notification messages right after an eligible purchase.
contingency.ifB: If it's cost perception or hassle, the message needs to address that directly (cost transparency, one-tap conversion) rather than just notify.
contingency.ifUnknown: If you don't know, I'll design the message to cover both awareness and reassurance, and use the first run to see which barrier is really driving non-conversion.

limitations: Stated as unavailable by the user: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.

dimensions.name: Transaction size (₹10,000+ vs below)
dimensions.rationale: Large-ticket eligible transactions already convert more; since the goal is maximising the count of conversions, the real opportunity is the smaller-ticket eligible transactions that are not converting today, and the message may need to work harder for them.
dimensions.note: User-reported pattern, not measured data (no campaign or transaction history exists yet). Used to decide where the campaign's effort is most needed, not to exclude anyone — all eligible transactions stay in scope. This is the user's own explanation, carried as a hypothesis: it has not been tested and competing explanations may remain.

dimensions.name: Time elapsed since the eligible transaction (within the 7-day conversion window)
dimensions.rationale: An EMI request tied to a transaction expires 7 days after authorization, so how many days have passed since the purchase determines both how urgent the message should be and whether the customer can still act at all.
dimensions.note: Platform fact, not something to ask the manager. Sets the entry trigger and cadence for the journey.

dimensions.name: Purchase category or merchant
dimensions.rationale: Category could plausibly affect willingness to split a purchase into EMI, and competes with merchant-side EMI offers at checkout.
dimensions.note: Not raised when asked what else splits who converts, and not tracked. Not pursued this round; worth revisiting only if the first run's results can't be explained by ticket size and awareness alone.

successCriteria: Success is judged by the number of eligible transactions converted to EMI — a count, not the total value converted.

converters.shape: Eligible transactions of ₹10,000 and above convert to EMI at a higher rate than smaller eligible transactions.

candidates.why: Manager reports these already convert more often without prompting.

barriers.statement: Customers don't know whether a specific purchase actually qualifies for EMI conversion.
barriers.quote: they dont know if txn is eligible for emi or not
